text_blocks.snippet: The Johnson & Johnson (Janssen) COVID-19 vaccine is no longer available in the U.S.. It expired on May 6, 2023. Individuals who previously received the J&J vaccine are considered up-to-date when they follow recommendations for currently available updated vaccines.

The J&J vaccine was associated with a rare but serious side effect called thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome (TTS), characterized by blood clots and low blood platelet counts. The CDC reported that as of March 18, 2023, there were 60 reported cases of TTS, with nine deaths. The risk was found to be highest in women ages 30 to 49. Anyone experiencing symptoms like severe headaches, shortness of breath, chest pain, or other signs of blood clots after vaccination was advised to seek immediate medical care.

text_blocks.snippet: The Johnson & Johnson (J&J) COVID-19 vaccine is a single-dose vaccine that was developed to prevent COVID-19 infection. It is an adenovirus vector vaccine, which means it uses a harmless virus (adenovirus) to deliver the genetic instructions for the body to make the COVID-19 spike protein. This allows the body to develop an immune response to the virus without getting sick.

Clinical trials showed that the J&J vaccine was 66% effective in preventing moderate to severe COVID-19 infection 2 weeks after vaccination. It was also 85% effective in preventing hospitalization and death.

The J&J vaccine was authorized for emergency use in the United States in February 2021. However, as of May 2023, the vaccine is no longer available in the U.S. due to the expiration of its emergency use authorization.

list.snippet: The J&J vaccine is recommended for adults 18 years of age and older.
Side effects of the J&J vaccine are typically mild and include pain, redness, and swelling at the injection site, as well as headache, fatigue, and muscle aches.
